operations.name: Noel Colón Martínez

expected.name: Noel Colón Martínez
expected.description:
Noel Colón Martínez was a Puerto Rican lawyer, former president of the Puerto Rico Bar Association and advocate for Puerto Rico’s self-determination. A firsthand family interview identifies an August 2, 2001 arrest during civil disobedience against the U.S. Navy in Vieques. A commemorative lecture by Alejandro Torres Rivera describes imprisonment at MDC Guaynabo together with a son and grandson, linking three generations of the Colón family in the Vieques struggle.

The Bar Association records Colón’s birth in Moca on October 20, 1927 and death in San Juan on October 7, 2022. The cited custody accounts do not establish an individual sentence, prison admission date or release date.

operations.name: Leo Bazile

expected.name: Leo Bazile
expected.description: Leo Bazile was a former chair of the Black Student Union at Stanford University. Authorities issued warrants for Bazile and Black Liberation Front member Chris Laury on May 4, 1971, accusing them of assaulting Stanford Hospital clerk Mary Jane Schmidt during a labor dispute. Bazile was arrested and initially held on $12,500 bail, later reduced to $6,250. Their defense showed that Schmidt had selected Bazile from photographs before a lineup and misidentified another man when asked to identify Laury in court. A jury acquitted Bazile and Laury of every charge. The available record does not establish Bazile’s exact booking and release dates.
